newsitem.title: UK: U-Freight boss highlights problems in airfreight industry.
newsitem.headline: U-Freight boss highlights problems in airfreight industry.

text.p: The level of rates is by far the most serious of several problems the global airfreight industry needs to address if it is to stay competitive and improve the quality of, U-Freight America's president Gene Boyer said in a recent speech.

"As an airfreight forwarder we are in a no win position trying to balance the demands of shippers for ever lower rates and the needs of airlines for firmer tariffs," the logistics group executive said.

"One possible way through this dilemma is by making greater use of technology with forwarders and airlines having wider access to their respective systems so as to be able to reduce overheads", Boyer.stated.
Maintaining and improving levels of quality is one key area facing the airfreight industry in the future as customers are increasingly aware of quality.
The other long running area is the battle between the integrators and forwarders.

"Both parties have their particular expertise which is fine so long as each party stays within them," says Boyer. "The integrators are best at catering for the small express shipments but more and more they are now handling heavier shipments, which have traditionally been the preserve of the forwarders.

"In turn, the forwarders have moved into the smaller weight bands and express shipments to compete with the integrators in trying to provide a single source meeting all the transport needs of one customer."
"Competition is the driving force here so it is unlikely an acceptable solution is forthcoming," Boyer added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
